stem: An integer sequence starts x_0=6, x_1=5. For n >= 2, x_n is the least nonnegative residue of 1*x_(n-1) + 2*x_(n-2) modulo 23. What is x_9?
An integer sequence starts x_0=3, x_1=2. For n >= 2, x_n is the least nonnegative residue of 2*x_(n-1) + 2*x_(n-2) modulo 17. What is x_10?
An integer sequence starts x_0=1, x_1=4. For n >= 2, x_n is the least nonnegative residue of 3*x_(n-1) + 1*x_(n-2) modulo 19. What is x_10?
An integer sequence starts x_0=2, x_1=2. For n >= 2, x_n is the least nonnegative residue of 3*x_(n-1) + 1*x_(n-2) modulo 19. What is x_8?

Six distinct labeled objects have weights [3, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13] in label order. How many unordered subsets of exactly three objects have total weight at most 23 and congruent to 0 modulo 4? Each object is available once; count subsets, not ordered selections.

Six distinct labeled objects have weights [3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14] in label order. How many unordered subsets of exactly three objects have total weight at most 20 and congruent to 2 modulo 3? Each object is available once; count subsets, not ordered selections.

Six distinct labeled objects have weights [3, 4, 8, 13, 14, 15] in label order. How many unordered subsets of exactly three objects have total weight at most 25 and congruent to 1 modulo 4? Each object is available once; count subsets, not ordered selections.

Six distinct labeled objects have weights [2, 3, 8, 9, 11, 13] in label order. How many unordered subsets of exactly three objects have total weight at most 27 and congruent to 1 modulo 3? Each object is available once; count subsets, not ordered selections.

A directed graph has vertices 0 through 5. Each [u,v,w] entry is an edge u -> v with cost w. There are no other edges; reverse edges are not implied. Edges: [[0, 1, 2], [0, 5, 3], [1, 2, 7], [1, 4, 8], [2, 3, 6], [2, 5, 5], [3, 4, 9], [3, 5, 11], [4, 5, 8]]. What is the minimum total cost of a path from vertex 0 to vertex 5?

Edges: [[0, 1, 9], [0, 3, 10], [0, 4, 7], [1, 2, 12], [2, 3, 8], [3, 4, 12], [3, 5, 5], [4, 5, 5]]. What is the minimum total cost of a path from vertex 0 to vertex 5?

What is the minimum total cost of a path from vertex 0 to vertex 5?

Edges: [[0, 1, 10], [0, 2, 9], [0, 3, 5], [0, 4, 12], [0, 5, 2], [1, 2, 3], [1, 4, 6], [2, 3, 8], [2, 4, 7], [2, 5, 2], [3, 4, 4], [3, 5, 8], [4, 5, 9]]. What is the minimum total cost of a path from vertex 0 to vertex 5?

Choose urn U with probability 1/3, otherwise urn V. U contains 5 red and 6 blue balls; V contains 3 red and 3 blue balls. Draw 3 balls uniformly without replacement from the chosen urn and observe exactly one red and 2 blue, with order unobserved. Which option is the posterior probability that U was chosen, rounded to the nearest whole percentage point (round a half percentage point upward)?

Choose urn U with probability 1/3, otherwise urn V. U contains 3 red and 3 blue balls; V contains 6 red and 4 blue balls. Draw 2 balls uniformly without replacement from the chosen urn and observe exactly one red and 1 blue, with order unobserved. Which option is the posterior probability that U was chosen, rounded to the nearest whole percentage point (round a half percentage point upward)?

Choose urn U with probability 1/3, otherwise urn V. U contains 7 red and 3 blue balls; V contains 4 red and 7 blue balls. Draw 3 balls uniformly without replacement from the chosen urn and observe exactly one red and 2 blue, with order unobserved. Which option is the posterior probability that U was chosen, rounded to the nearest whole percentage point (round a half percentage point upward)?

Choose urn U with probability 2/3, otherwise urn V. U contains 6 red and 6 blue balls; V contains 6 red and 4 blue balls. Draw 2 balls uniformly without replacement from the chosen urn and observe exactly one red and 1 blue, with order unobserved. Which option is the posterior probability that U was chosen, rounded to the nearest whole percentage point (round a half percentage point upward)?
